title: Private deployment packaging: helm chart updates + installer wiring for audit-export components (document network egress)
creator: Benji Okafor
description:
Goal
Enable SIEM-ready audit export (beta) in Redwood Private deployments by wiring the exporter components into the private installer and Helm charts, including clear documentation for required outbound network egress (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3) and constrained-network options.

Context
Private customers frequently run with default-deny egress policies and strict TLS interception/custom CAs. For beta, we need predictable install/upgrade behavior and explicit guidance on what outbound connections are required per sink, plus how to validate connectivity.

Scope
1) Helm chart updates (redwood-private / audit-exporter)
- Add audit-export worker deployment + supporting K8s objects to Private Helm bundle.
- Ensure separation of concerns:
  - control plane config served by redwood-control-plane (existing)
  - delivery workers run as separate deployment (audit-export-worker) with bounded resource usage
- Add values schema for:
  - enabling/disabling audit export subsystem
  - sink toggles (splunk/datadog/s3 enabled)
  - proxy support (HTTP(S)_PROXY + NO_PROXY)
  - custom CA bundle mount (optional)
  - resource requests/limits and concurrency knobs (safe defaults)
  - DLQ retention settings (if applicable in Private)
- RBAC:
  - serviceAccount + role/roleBinding limited to required namespaces/resources
  - no cluster-admin assumptions
- Secrets:
  - reference to Private secrets integration pattern (Vault/K8s secret + sealed secrets depending on deployment)
  - ensure destination credentials are stored/managed in control plane secrets store; workers should only receive short-lived access tokens/refs where possible

2) Private installer wiring (redwood-private-installer)
- Add installer flags/config to enable audit export components.
- Add preflight checks:
  - DNS resolution
  - outbound connectivity to configured sink endpoints
  - bucket write permissions for S3 sink when enabled (best-effort validation)
- Ensure upgrade safety:
  - installs cleanly when feature flag is disabled
  - upgrades don’t break clusters that don’t enable SIEM export
  - chart supports rolling upgrades with minimal downtime (workers can restart; at-least-once semantics tolerate retries)

3) Documentation: required network egress + constrained network guidance
- Add a Private-specific doc section covering outbound egress requirements:
  - Splunk HEC: customer-defined URL (often https://splunk.company.com:8088)
  - Datadog Logs intake: region-specific endpoints (e.g., https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com, gov/eu variants) customer-defined
  - S3: AWS S3 endpoint for region OR S3-compatible storage endpoint (customer-defined), plus KMS endpoint if using SSE-KMS
- Include examples for Kubernetes NetworkPolicy allowlists and/or firewall rules (high-level, not vendor-specific).
- TLS guidance:
  - required TLS versions (>=1.2)
  - custom CA bundle configuration if enterprise TLS intercept is used
  - certificate verification is enforced; no “insecure” mode for beta
- Proxy guidance:
  - supported env vars for worker pods
  - ensure NO_PROXY covers in-cluster services
- Validation / troubleshooting steps:
  - installer preflight
  - curl/wget checks from a debug pod
  - reading worker logs and interpreting common errors (x509 unknown authority, i/o timeout, 401/403)

Non-goals (beta)
- Full air-gapped export (no external egress) beyond S3-compatible in-cluster endpoint.
- Supporting every service mesh/TLS sidecar configuration; provide best-effort guidance and document known caveats.
- Building a UI in the Private installer (CLI/config only).

Acceptance criteria
- Private installer can deploy audit-export worker components behind a feature flag.
- Helm values documented with safe defaults.
- Documented egress requirements per sink + proxy/custom CA instructions.
- Preflight checks catch obvious misconfigurations (missing DNS, blocked egress) with actionable messages.
- Verified on at least one restricted egress test cluster (network policy default deny) in staging.

Implementation notes / links
- Related PR (Private installer wiring): sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr_0273.json
- Terraform examples (S3 IAM/KMS guidance may be referenced in docs): sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr_0440.json
- Private install notes draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/private-siem-export-install-notes.json

Open questions
- Do we mandate a single worker deployment per tenant, or per destination? (current assumption: per tenant, multi-destination via config; re-evaluate if resource isolation is required for Private)
- Do we require explicit network egress allowlisting validation in installer, or make it best-effort and rely on runbook?
- How are destination credentials surfaced to workers in Private: direct K8s secret mount vs control-plane secret fetch with scoped token? (Security prefers control-plane fetch; confirm implementation status in ENG-13933)

Rollout
- Behind per-tenant feature flag in Private. Default off.
- Enable on 1 internal Private staging cluster; run soak test with Splunk mock + S3 minio.
- Enable for 1 beta Private design partner with Solutions Eng support and a “network egress checklist” as part of onboarding.
comments:
2025-02-10 (Diego Santos)
Starting with chart changes. Plan is to keep the worker as a separate Deployment in the private bundle (same pattern as other auxiliary subsystems). Will add values for proxy + custom CA because Private customers asked for it repeatedly.

I’ll sync with Hanae on how we should reference credentials: control-plane secret store vs K8s secret mount. My assumption is workers fetch via control-plane with scoped token to avoid duplicating secrets in multiple places.

Next: draft egress doc section + add installer preflight skeleton.

2025-02-13 (Hanae Suzuki)
Security note: please do NOT add an “insecureSkipVerify” knob for beta. If customers have TLS interception, we should support custom CA bundle injection and keep verification enabled.

For secret flow: OK with workers using a short-lived token to read destination creds from control-plane secret store. If we must mount anything into the pod, it should be only the token (scoped) and not the raw destination credentials.

Also: ensure RBAC for the worker SA cannot list/read unrelated secrets in the namespace.

2025-02-18 (Colin O'Donnell)
Customer signal (Private design partner): default-deny egress with explicit allowlist. They need a clear one-pager: “what domains/ports must be reachable” + how to test from inside the cluster. For Splunk it’s an internal endpoint, for S3 it might be an on-prem S3-compatible store.

They also asked if Datadog is optional (yes) and whether we can route via HTTPS proxy (strong +1).

2025-02-24 (Connor O'Brien)
Release engineering: please ensure installer upgrade path is no-op when SIEM export is disabled, and add a guard so we don’t accidentally start workers without control-plane config ready.

For beta launch checklist we need: (1) versioned chart values documented, (2) preflight errors are copy/pasteable into support tickets, (3) rollback tested (disable feature flag + scale worker to 0).

2025-03-04 (Diego Santos)
Progress update:
- Helm chart: added audit-export-worker Deployment + ServiceAccount + Role/RoleBinding. Defaults set to low concurrency with CPU/mem requests to avoid impacting core services.
- Added support for HTTP(S)_PROXY and custom CA bundle volume mount (optional).
- Installer: added config wiring + basic DNS/egress preflight hooks (needs error message polish).
- Docs: drafted “Required network egress” section with sink-by-sink checklist; needs Security + Solutions review.

Remaining:
- Confirm secret/token flow with ENG-13933 implementation (don’t want to bake in wrong assumption).
- Add restricted-egress staging validation and record results.
- Finish doc examples for NetworkPolicy allowlist patterns (generic).
